kjv: [being] a chief man among his people
mine: as a husband among his people
note: Hebrew lo yittamma ba'al be'ammaw is terse and obscure; ba'al most often means "husband/owner", suggesting the priest may not defile himself for in-laws or a wife's kin (or as a husband), whereas the KJV takes ba'al as "chief man", a sense not otherwise attested for the word.
Hebrew lechem elohehem; lechem here denotes sacrificial food generally (chiefly meat and fat burned on the altar), not bread specifically (also vv. 8, 17, 21, 22).

mine: shall not let the hair of his head hang loose
note: Hebrew et-rosho lo yifra', from para' "let loose/dishevel", a mourning gesture (cf. 10:6, 13:45); the issue is unbound hair, not removing a head covering.

kjv: the crown of the anointing oil
mine: the consecration of the anointing oil
note: Hebrew nezer means both "consecration/dedication" and the "crown/diadem" that marks it; here it is the anointing oil itself, so "consecration" fits the phrase better.

kjv: he that hath a flat nose, or any thing superfluous
mine: has a disfigured face or a limb too long
note: Hebrew harum and saru'a are rare; harum is probably a facial disfigurement (traditionally a split or flat nose) and saru'a "overgrown/elongated" (a deformed limb); the KJV's "any thing superfluous" is vague.

mine: or an itching disease or scabs
note: Hebrew garav and yallefet are skin diseases (eczema, scabs); "scurvy" now names a vitamin-deficiency disease.
